progress.summary: Global inventory of major AI/hyperscale data centers quantified in H100e, plus US utility-territory impacts (energy prices and water) and an operator-efficiency comparison. Current release: 442 sites, 71 countries, ~64.0M H100e, 121 US sites across 55 utility territories, 13 operators.

entry.title: Prose rewritten in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100)
entry.detail:
Installed the asd-ste100 skill under .opencode/skills/asd-ste100 and rewrote the seven markdown docs plus the dashboard copy. The bundled linter (ste-lint.py --baseline 9999) reports 0 violations across 11,757 words, down from 305 baseline violations: README 69, us_water_energy 56, us_impacts_verification 50, gpu_cooling 36, DATA_DICTIONARY 33, AGENTS 32, operator_efficiency 29.
Scope: README, AGENTS, DATA_DICTIONARY, the four docs, and the user-facing strings in pipeline/frontend/index.template.html and pipeline/frontend/dashboard.js. PROGRESS.xml history and Python comments/docstrings were left alone. Every fact, number, source URL, table row, grade and caveat was preserved. Element IDs, data attributes and JS identifiers are unchanged.
Also corrected two stale figures in AGENTS.md section 8 and the PROGRESS state block: status counts are 199/35/117/91 (not 116/92) and total H100e is ~64.0M (not 64.7M). Both now match data/published/data_centers.csv, which is the source of truth.

entry.title: Site-efficiency view: all 442 campuses scored on disclosed evidence
entry.detail:
Added a third dashboard section (03 / SITE EFFICIENCY) that asks the operator chart's question of every campus, and states how few can answer it. Coverage strip: 442 tracked, 307 with a power denominator, 127 with an operator-disclosed PUE, 93 with a water intensity, 51 with an accelerator-heat estimate, 135 with no power denominator.
Chart axes were changed from "cooling % x water" to "operator-disclosed PUE x water intensity" during the build. PUE is populated for all 442 rows, but 315 of them carry the industry default 1.20 rather than a disclosure, so a cooling-percentage axis was fabricated for 71% of the dataset. pipeline/dashboard.py now emits a pue_disclosed flag and the chart plots only the 127 rows where it is true (88 once a water figure is also required).
Those 88 campuses collapse onto six distinct (PUE, water, rejection) positions - Google 26, Meta 20, Microsoft 19, AWS 14, Nebius 5, Crusoe 4 - because a site's PUE is its operator's fleet figure and its water is the operator's fleet WUE applied to site IT load. Bubbles are sized by the number of campuses at a position, so the clustering is the finding rather than an overlap artefact. Grouping keys on the rounded pixel position, not the raw value: operator intensities differ in the fourth decimal (8.9345 vs 8.9394 ML/MW-yr) and value equality stacked two bubbles on one pixel.
The rack-cooling x heat-rejection matrix covers all 442 sites and does stay per-site: 36 evaporative with no rack evidence, 39 direct-to-chip with unknown rejection, 34 naming both layers. A sortable, searchable, filterable ledger lists all 442 with IT MW, H100e/MW, PUE, water intensity, rack, rejection and confidence; default sort is IT load descending, and PUE values that are the industry default carry a *. Waterless sites are kept at 0 in the ledger and excluded from the log-axis scatter. Water figures resting on a stated WUE estimate rather than a disclosure (the two xAI rows, 1.0 L/kWh) carry a ≈ in the ledger.
Plumbing: shared bundling extracted to pipeline/dashboard.py so both build.py and build_gpu_cooling.py refresh index.html with current data; build.py now injects typed JSON instead of in-memory string rows.

entry.title: Per-site accelerator and cooling dataset with water caveats
entry.detail: Added data/gpu_platforms.csv (41 accelerator platforms: TDP, rack system, rack cooling, heat-to-liquid share, source, match rule) and a generated data/gpu_cooling.csv/.json covering all 442 sites, built by pipeline/build_gpu_cooling.py. The study separates rack cooling (air, direct-to-chip, immersion) from facility heat rejection (evaporative, dry closed loop, hybrid) and rejects the premise that the accelerator vendor determines water use. Formulas: accelerator heat = count x TDP / 1e6; cooling thermal load ~= IT load; cooling electricity = IT load x (PUE - 1); water = IT MW x 8,760 x 1,000 x operator fleet WUE. Mixed generations get a TDP/heat range, never a single point. Coverage: 177 sites with a named platform (158 from gpu_types, 19 from notes), 74 with an announced count, 51 with an accelerator-heat estimate (36 single TDP, 15 ranged), 307 with IT load and cooling electricity, 94 with a fleet-scaled water estimate. Hardware confidence B 38 / C 66 / D 338 and no A, because no site combines an official TDP, a published count and site-specific cooling evidence. Four explicitly waterless sites carry zero water and negligible dependency. Three rows keep heat-above-IT-load warnings (Meta Prometheus, JUPITER, Domyn Colosseum) rather than being silently corrected. No water figure is presented as a site measurement.

entry.title: Compute Atlas interactive efficiency dashboard
entry.detail: Replaced the map-only page with a responsive, data-driven dashboard. The global atlas now supports text, country and status filters, H100e or power marker sizing, site evidence profiles, a filter-linked leaderboard and CSV selection export. Operator efficiency is explained through an interactive PUE/WUE scatter plot, disclosure-boundary profiles, a full disclosure table and a two-operator annual energy/water scenario lab. Reporting-year, scope, withdrawal/consumption and design-target caveats remain adjacent to the visual claims. Reusable HTML/CSS/JS sources live in pipeline/frontend and are embedded by build.py; no research values or canonical rows changed. Browser checks passed for filtering, site and operator selection, scenario arithmetic, console errors and horizontal overflow at 1440px and 390px.

entry.title: Full corpus verification: 510 rows checked against sources
entry.detail: All 442 site rows, all 55 utility rows and all 13 operator rows were checked against their cited sources by 15 parallel research agents, plus a script pass over the derived arithmetic (status totals, H100e sums, GPU conversion factors, method priority) and all 623 cited URLs. Result: 402 SUPPORTED, 99 PARTLY_SUPPORTED, 9 CONTRADICTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. Per-row record: data/verification/verdicts.csv. Summary and corrections table: docs/verification_ledger.md. Corrections applied: 9 contradicted rows fixed (AWS Madison County 2200->1000 MW; Google Midlothian third-party 331,986->143,581; TeraWulf row split from the Hawesville Anthropic lease and renamed to Lake Hawkeye; Fairwater Atlanta moved to Fayetteville/640 MW/150k GB200; China Telecom Qingyang 250->135 MW; Bridge Cyberjaya 98->20 MW; Nebius Beit Shemesh 80->58 MW; China Mobile Hohhot 10,000->20,000 cards; Data Vault Pakistan 3,000->100 GPUs; FirstEnergy Ohio 2025 increase 7.1%>11.8%/13.3%), 2 mis-cited source URLs replaced (Google West Memphis, Bitdeer Milam County), and 8 dead links replaced (all replacements verified HTTP 200). Headline totals changed: ~64.0M H100e (was ~64.7M); status split now 199/35/117/91 (Google West Memphis planned -> under_construction).

entry.title: Repository reorganised into data / pipeline / docs
entry.detail: Flat layout replaced with a structured one before the first commit: data/{canonical,raw,published}, pipeline/{,archive,verification}, docs/. The canonical dataset moved from data_centers_fixed.csv to data/canonical/data_centers.csv; build outputs now live in data/published/ and index.html stays at the repo root for GitHub Pages. Every script now derives ROOT from __file__, so it runs from any working directory. Country count corrected from 69 to 71 (71 distinct country strings in the canonical data; the old figure was stale).

entry.title: Archive scripts truncated by a rewrite bug; recovered intact
entry.detail: During the restructure a one-line Python rewrite opened each pipeline/archive/*.py for writing before reading it, truncating all nine scripts to zero bytes. The canonical dataset, published outputs and all documents were unaffected. The original tool-call payloads were still in OpenCode's local session database, so all nine files were rebuilt and verified byte-for-byte against their pre-incident sizes, then re-patched for the new paths. Guardrail: read a file fully into memory before opening it for write; never call open(path, "w") as the object of a method whose argument re-reads the same path.

entry.title: Scripts resolve the repo root from their own location
entry.detail: All pipeline scripts compute ROOT from __file__ (one level for pipeline/*.py, two for pipeline/archive and pipeline/verification) and build absolute paths from it. This makes the layout reorganisation safe and lets scripts run from any working directory. New scripts must follow the same pattern.

entry.title: Repository packaged and published
entry.detail: Initial public packaging: AGENTS.md, PROGRESS.xml, DATA_DICTIONARY.md, .gitignore and a token-safe push helper. Dataset, map, US impacts study and operator-efficiency study committed together. Remote: github.com/tedngai/datacenter-efficiency-study (branch main).

entry.title: Credentials never enter tracked files
entry.detail: The GitHub PAT lives only in .env (gitignored). AGENTS.md documents the location and handling, not the value. Pushes use scripts/push.ps1, which reads .env at runtime, disables the credential helper and targets a tokenised URL so nothing is written to .git/config. Rationale: a token in git history is compromised even after deletion, and this repository is published.

entry.title: Operator efficiency comparison added
entry.detail: Built operator_efficiency.csv (13 operators) and operator_efficiency.md. Fleet metrics: Meta PUE 1.08 / WUE 0.19 (2024); Google 1.09 / 1.02 derived (2025); AWS 1.14 / 0.12 (2025); Microsoft 1.17 / 0.27 (FY25). Key finding: energy and water trade off — Google has the best PUE of the largest fleet but 5-8x the water intensity of Meta/AWS. Neoclouds split into design claims (Crusoe, Nebius) and non-disclosure (CoreWeave, Applied Digital, Lambda, Galaxy); xAI discloses nothing, bottom-up estimate ~1.0 L/kWh.

entry.title: Dominion order dated and described incorrectly
entry.detail: Row text said "Jan 2026 order" and "14-yr contracts". The SCC final order is dated 25 Nov 2025 (PUR-2025-00058) and the release contains no 14-year term; the minimums are 85% distribution/transmission and 60% generation. Corrected in the NoVA row and in us_water_energy.md.

entry.title: Two water figures downgraded to unverified
entry.detail: AWS Ridgeland's 3.67 MGD peak-day demand does not appear in the water-service agreement text; xAI's 1.3 MGD contract demand rests on a paywalled Commercial Appeal piece. Both rows now say "reported, unverified" instead of asserting the figure.

entry.title: Fermi water rate overstated as 'double the standard rate'
entry.detail: Amarillo reporting confirms $8.72 per 1,000 gallons and that it is the highest industrial rate the city has ever charged; it does not support "double". Corrected in both the CSV and the report table.

entry.title: Microsoft Goodyear water allowance mischaracterised
entry.detail: The 1.2 MGD in the 2023 council amendment is wastewater treatment capacity, not a freshwater entitlement. The original cooling plan was up to 5 MGD (~1M gpd per building); later buildings were switched to air cooling. Row rewritten with the $36M contribution to the $90M plant.

entry.title: Alabama price comparison had the sign wrong
entry.detail: Montgomery was described as above the US average (13.09c vs 16.48c). EIA shows 12.96c (2021) and 16.09c (2025) against a 17.23c US average — below, not above. High Alabama bills come from consumption per household, not price per kWh. Row corrected and the distinction made explicit.

entry.title: Systematic 2021 price baselines ~1c/kWh too low
entry.detail: Subagent-supplied 2021 baselines were consistently low (VA 11.0 vs 11.96; AR 9.9 vs 11.27; GA 11.7 vs 12.51; AZ 11.7 vs 12.54), and several 2025 figures were mid-year quotes or "typical bill / 1,000 kWh" arithmetic. All 32 state series re-based on EIA Table 2.10 (2021, 2024, 2025) and EEM Table 5.6.B (Jan-Aug 2026 YTD). A Wyoming "9.14c in 2024" claim could not be reconciled and was removed.

entry.title: US price and water claims verified; grades assigned
entry.detail: Load-bearing claims checked against EIA, Google 2026 Environmental Report p.97, Virginia SCC, PJM BRA, Georgia PSC rate survey, Wisconsin PSC 5-UR-111/112 and Umatilla notices. Grades: 25 A, 30 B, 0 C, 0 D. Four correction passes applied (verify_apply.py to verify_apply4.py), each printing OK/MISS per edit.

entry.title: Google site water re-based on 2026 Environmental Report
entry.detail: Council Bluffs corrected from "~1.4B gal (2024)" to 1,746.4M withdrawn / 1,346.0M consumed (2025). New Albany corrected from "~127M gal/yr" to 1,008.1M / 835.7M. Google Nebraska corrected to 732.1M consumed in 2025, up from 134.7M in 2023 (not 2024). Loudoun clarified as 899M potable plus 815M reclaimed.

entry.title: Group US impacts by utility territory, not by site
entry.detail: 121 US sites collapse into 55 utility territories; grouping avoids repeating the same rate case and water source dozens of times. One row per territory, listing the sites it covers.

entry.title: Boydton attributed to the wrong utility
entry.detail: Microsoft Boydton was attributed to AEP Virginia. EIA territory data shows Mecklenburg Electric Cooperative / Southside Electric Cooperative with some Dominion. A 2021 MEC SCC filing confirms a data-center special rate in its territory. Dataset and US impacts row corrected.

entry.title: Nscale NC-1 located in the wrong county
entry.detail: Corrected to the town of Madison, Rockingham County, North Carolina (Duke Energy Carolinas territory), not Madison County.

entry.title: Cipher Barber Lake placed in the wrong state
entry.detail: Listed in Barbour County, West Virginia; it is in Colorado City, Texas (Cipher 8-K, Sep 2025). Row corrected; the WV Mon Power row in the US impacts file is retained only as regional context.

entry.detail: Added H100e methodology, status table, regional coverage note and the country-level summary table generated from h100e_best.

entry.detail: us_utility_impacts.csv (55 territory rows) and us_water_energy.md (headline findings, big-drinker table, complaint groups, caveats) built from six regional research sweeps covering all 121 US sites.

entry.detail: Regional deep-dives merged into the canonical dataset, reaching 442 sites across 69 countries. Status coverage validated by build.py.

entry.title: Four-state status taxonomy with fixed map colours
entry.detail: operational / partially_operational / under_construction / planned map to green / yellow / blue / purple on the Leaflet map. Any new status value requires updating build.py, the legend and this document.

entry.title: H100e computed three ways, best estimate published
entry.detail: h100e_gpu (count conversion), h100e_flops (peak FLOPS) and h100e_power (500 per MW IT, 417 per MW gross at PUE 1.2). h100e_best picks the strongest available method and h100e_method records which one. Mixed GPU generations get no single factor and are left blank with a note.

entry.title: GPU generation conversion factors fixed
Inclusion bar set at ~100 MW or 10k+ GPUs
entry.detail: Major AI/hyperscale campuses only. National-lab supercomputers excluded except where genuinely notable as AI systems. Thin rows kept when the site is notable, with an honest note; overlapping or uncertain sites kept with an explicit warning note rather than silently dropped.

entry.title: PowerShell quoting and download-path failures during verification
entry.detail: Inline Python f-strings broke under PowerShell 5 parsing, and EIA files downloaded under URL-derived names did not match the expected paths. Fix: write verification logic to .py files and reference explicit filenames. Also, the first correction pass used guessed substrings and reported MISS on 13 edits; the second pass used exact substrings from the CSV.
